newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PDVSA DECLARES FORCE MAJEURE ON GASOLINE CARGOES.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA DECLARES FORCE MAJEURE ON GASOLINE CARGOES.

text.p: Venezuela's state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) declared force majeure on two or three gasoline cargoes after a 60,000 barrel per day reformer at the Cardon refinery ran into problems, a Venezuelan trader said on Wednesday.
He said reformer throughput was lower than normal and it was only producing low octane gasoline which did not conform to previous sales specifications.
"It is not shut down, it is just not producing the octane level we normally use in our blending of mogas. As a consequence we are short of octanes," he said.
The cancelled cargoes contain 230,000 barrels each.
The trader said there had been no force majeure called yet on gasoline exports from the fire-striken Curacao refinery yet, but this was still a possibility.
"Up to now they have been able to supply committments that were nominated and accepted. I think if the situation at Cardon stays the same, it might happen (in Curacao)," he said.
The Cardon and Curacao refineries are major suppliers of refined oil products to the U.S. market.
